summary: B is preferable because it is narrower, keeps request/response handling shared, and tests retrying an upload sourced from an os.File. It still needs changes before merge because it alters Add and does not route Upload through Add as required.
reasons: B reuses multipartbody.NewFile with the required field name and exact Upload signature.
B's os.File retry test verifies filename and content on both sides of a 429 retry.
B centralizes option handling, request construction, and decoding in add; A duplicates the existing Add implementation inside Upload.
A introduces broad RawClient replay and reader-ownership changes affecting Add, Update, and other seekable request bodies, despite the contract excluding retry refactoring.
risks_a: Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of FilesService.Add, duplicating request and response logic.
enableBodyReplay changes global retry and Close semantics for seekable readers and shares one mutable seeker across GetBody calls.
No test covers propagation of an Upload source-reader failure.
risks_b: Add now buffers every caller-provided body with io.ReadAll, changing its established streaming, memory, error-wrapping, and reader-closing behavior.
Upload calls the extracted private add method rather than the required existing Add method.
Tests omit empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader-error cases.
